summary: Polygon's Charlie Hall gathered picks from nearly two dozen tabletop writers, designers, and personalities on the TTRPGs that made an impact in 2023. The list spans lightweight storytelling games, LARPs, solo journaling games, horror, superhero RPGs, and bestiary supplements. The intro notes that tabletop role-play is having a moment after D&D's OGL fiasco, with The Quiet Year and The One Ring returning from last year's list.
one_line: Polygon's 2023 roundup of the best tabletop RPGs, as chosen by nearly two dozen designers, writers, and personalities in the hobby.
key_facts: Polygon asked nearly two dozen writers, designers, presenters, actors, and personalities from tabletop gaming to name the TTRPGs that mattered to them in 2023.
The Quiet Year and The One Ring both make their second appearance on the list; The Quiet Year was on last year's roundup too.
Linda Codega picked City of Winter, a lightweight game played on a cloth map where players are a family of immigrants fleeing a darkness from the west and deciding which traditions to keep.
Jason Morningstar recommended Jenn Martin's Dead After Dinner, which combines For the Queen's procedural revelation with a Knives Out-style murder mystery.

Tim Hutchings called a tie between Desperation by Jason Morningstar, a card-driven TTRPG with two American Gothic scenarios, and Orestes' Choice by Susanne Vejdemo, a chamber LARP about a queer Greek myth.

Thilo Graf praised Dungeon Crawl Classics by Goodman Games for its volatile magic, flat power curve, and emphasis on player skill; it inspired his Survivalist's Guide to Spelunking for 5e, co-written with Douglas Niles and Stephen Yeardley.
Fetch My Blade, by Kelly Tran and Ethan Yen, is a 17-page solo journaling RPG in which you play the dog of a retired sword master, using three six-sided dice.
Home, by Doug Levandowski and Yeonsoo Julian Kim, is a haunted house game playable solo or with a group, driven by custom tarot cards called the Night Deck.

Masks of the Masks by Hazel Amber Goswick is an RPG presented as an illustrated comic book, blending Belonging Outside Belonging and Powered by the Apocalypse and homaging Bronze Age superhero stories.
Skerples' The Monster Overhaul is divided into 20 categories of 10 monsters each, including unusual ones like 'Summer' and 'A Wizard Did It'.
Triangle Agency is written as an employee handbook about containing Anomalies; its full release ships early in 2024, with digital rules available now at a pay-what-you-think-is-appropriate price.
Project ECCO is a solo time-travel and cosmic horror game played in a yearly planner, taking three to 10 hours per game.
Bianca Canoza (Momatoes), 2022 Diana Jones Emerging Designer award winner, created What Dust Remains, which Danny Quach played at Big Bad Con 2023.
The Wildsea by Felix Isaacs and Mythworks uses a d6 dice pool system and won an Ennie in 2023.
